text:
jess_support: Customer on prod reports SSE stream abruptly closes ~30s after start whenever the client's token refreshes. Request ID: rx-5b1f9c. Region: us-west-2. Model: redwood-13b-instruct. Client stderr shows an HTTP/1.1 401 mid-stream.

matt_infra: Can you paste the exact request-id header and the customer's curl? Also need LB/nginx logs for the 1812345678-1812345799 window.

jess_support: From the customer (redacted tokens):
```
curl -N -H \"Authorization: Bearer <token>\" -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream -d '{\"model\":\"redwood-13b-instruct\",\"input\":\"hello\"}'
```
Client SSE captured: 
```
data: {\"delta\":\"Hi\"}
data: {\"delta\":\" there\"}
event: error
data: {\"message\":\"unauthorized\",\"code\":401}
```

tim_runtime: Quick Qs: 1) Are they using rotating short-lived tokens? 2) Which SDK/proxy sits in front of the client? LB idle timeout could drop things when token refresh triggers a re-auth path.

matt_infra: Repro curl to run from their network or our jumpbox: 
```
curl -v --no-buffer -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TEST_TOKEN\" -H \"Connection: keep-alive\" --http2 -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream -d '{\"model\":\"redwood-13b-instruct\",\"input\":\"stream test\"}'
```
Include `-v` so we can see the server/proxy headers. If the customer uses cookie auth, try adding `-H \"Cookie: session=...\"`.

jess_support: Debug-bundle checklist for customer: nginx access + error logs (us-west-2) for the timeframe, ALB logs, token / OAuth refresh logs, client stderr/stdout, exact client clock skew, and the request tracer for rx-5b1f9c. Tar/gzip and drop to secure bucket, then paste link.

sre-bot: @matt_infra Created ticket INFR-402: potential idle-timeout + auth refresh handling. https://redwood.atlassian/INFR-402

tim_runtime: Also try reproducing with `curl --raw` and with/without `--no-buffer` to check how curl flushes chunks. SSE is sensitive to Transfer-Encoding chunked + keep-alive semantics.

carla_cs: I coordinated with the customer; they can run the curl test on Tuesday and will share logs. They consented to support access for a short window.

jess_support: I ran the repro from the support jumpbox using a token that expires in 60s. Observed same behavior: 401 emitted as an SSE error after ~33s. Server-side verbose: 
```
< HTTP/2 200
< content-type: text/event-stream
< transfer-encoding: chunked
...
< event: error
< data: {\"code\":401,\"message\":\"token_expired\"}
```

matt_infra: That matches my hypothesis — the auth middleware is returning a 401 mid-stream when it sees an expired/rotated token. Short-term mitigation: treat 401 during an active SSE stream as a non-terminal event (emit an SSE error event but don't immediately teardown the TCP connection), or require token refresh before starting a long-lived stream. I'll open a PR to adjust middleware behavior.

tim_runtime: PR #2134 opened to change auth behavior for streaming endpoints. Will canary in us-west-2 tomorrow 08:00 UTC; will monitor request id rx-5b1f9c and similar.

jess_support: Communicated workaround to customer: use a long-lived token or refresh token before initiating stream. Carla will coordinate test. I've asked them to upload the debug bundle when ready.

matt_infra: If the curl repro fails for some partners, try forcing HTTP/1.1 by removing `--http2` or adding `-H \"Upgrade: \"` to mimic their client. Some proxies downgrade or have different idle timeout behavior per protocol.

jess_support: Thanks — keeping this thread open until we get customer's debug bundle and validate the canary.

(emoji reactions: :thumbsup: on matt_infra, :eyes: on tim_runtime)
